key_insight: Structured LLM-guided threat modeling identifies smart-grid attack paths that better align with physics-grounded impact references while reducing analysis runtime.
engineering_relevance: The framework could help grid-security engineers prioritize high-impact cyber-physical attack scenarios for faster resilience assessment.
method: Combine system topology with LLM-guided STRIDE and MITRE ATT&CK threat modeling.
Use cascading-failure-derived impact rankings as physics-grounded references.
Compare against topology-driven, threat-driven, and fusion-based baselines.
evidence_signal: Reported cyber-layer critical-node overlap@3 rises from approximately 33% to as high as 100%, node-level similarity reaches 65%, and path-level alignment reaches 48%; runtime falls approximately 75–85% versus the fusion baseline on IEEE 14-bus.
watch_item: Generalization to larger operational grids remains unclear, and alignment with simulation-derived references does not establish real-world attack feasibility.
paper_title: LLM-Guided Cyber-Physical Attack Path Identification in Smart Grids
